sermon.title: God’s Magnifical House Part III
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In Part III of “God’s Magnifical House,” the speaker takes 1 Chronicles 22:5 and says the church must be built by God’s pattern. He says the glory came into the temple when the people praised God, that God’s house is now people as living stones, and that music, thanksgiving and participation are sacrifices to him. He closes with the power of the gospel over human intellect and the claim that miracles are for the church today.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. The recording does not state the speaker’s name; personal remarks (boyhood in Kentucky, his wife, his healing) match Pastor Kincer, but his name is not spoken, so Michael should confirm. This is Part III; the captions spell his word as “magnifico,” “magnifical” and “magnificent,” and “magnifico” was corrected to “magnifical,” matching the title. Garbled spots are marked [unclear] (“the [unclear] swam in the Bible,” “the [unclear] did swim the whale,” the Greek word for “share” in Hebrews 13:16 which sounds like “koinonia,” “this [unclear] of the Holy Spirit,” “you [unclear] Jesus,” and an opening phrase in the second paragraph). Reference notes: “Romans 5 15 4” is Romans 15:4; “First Corinthians 6 9” for “your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost” is 1 Corinthians 6:19; “Matthew 22:9” for “you are in error, not knowing the Scriptures” is Matthew 22:29; “John chapter 15 verse 51” is John 15:5; the quote “God… does not dwell in temples made with hands” he attributes to Isaiah, and Acts 17:24 is the verse shown; he cites “Psalms 150” and Genesis 1 in passing. He reads from a modern translation and the NKJV shown differs. Statements about Congress, chaplains and Bibles in the 1770s, the Supreme Court and 1962, and the origin of the “separation of church and state” phrase are his own historical claims and are not verified here. He also names a television commentator and a mention of Calvin, Wesley and Augustine (transcript only), speaks on evolution, other religions, and tells a personal health story and says he did not take the prescribed medicine; these are his own views and experience, not medical advice.

chunks.section_question: What does 1 Chronicles 22:5 say the Lord’s house will be?
chunks.short_answer: He reads that “the lord’s house shall be exceedingly” magnifical, “of fame and glory throughout all countries,” and recalls that earlier parts covered the fame of Jesus and the apostles. He says “miracles should be a normal part of the magnifical church,” pointing to Noah, the fiery furnace and Daniel.

chunks.section_question: What is the place of music, singing and praise in church?

faqs.question: What does he say about foreigners helping build the Lord’s house?
faqs.answer: He says “it is built by foreigners aliens illegals or other words not so perfect individuals… along with God’s chosen people.”

faqs.question: Why does he say churches should be alike, like a car sold around the world?
faqs.answer: He says “we don’t have magnificent churches anymore… you go to one church and it’s different than the next church,” when “we should be like the Toyota car,” the same product anywhere. He says “we have got to get the vision for God’s way God’s pattern.”

faqs.question: What does he list as the parts of the temple?
faqs.answer: He lists “a door which is Jesus,” an altar for “the cleansing of sin that’s the cross,” a laver for “water baptism,” a lampstand, a table for “communion,” an altar of incense for “prayer and praise,” and “a holy of holies where God dwelt.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: indeed it came to pass, when the trumpeters and singers were as one, to make one sound to be heard in praising and thanking the LORD, and when they lifted up their voice with the trumpets and cymbals and instruments of music, and praised the LORD, saying: “For He is good, For His mercy endures forever,” that the house, the house of the LORD, was filled with a cloud, so that the priests could not continue ministering because of the cloud; for the glory of the LORD filled the house of God.

faqs.question: What does he say “know” means in John 17:3?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus gives “another definition of eternal life,” and that “know” is “used in the Bible as a sexual relationship,” so we are “to have an intimate relationship with God… it’s a real thing it’s not just head knowledge.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent.

faqs.question: Does he say the Bible is a book of faith?
faqs.answer: No. He says “the Bible is not a book of faith it never says it’s a book of faith,” but “a book of truth” that “leads you to God so you can know God.”

faqs.question: Why does he say there is a pause between songs?
faqs.answer: He says it is “a pause in between songs that people can lift up their song and sing and thank God their own personal self,” so “you’re not stuck with just chorus after chorus.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: But the hour is coming, and now is, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth; for the Father is seeking such to worship Him. God is Spirit, and those who worship Him must worship in spirit and truth.”

faqs.question: What does he say about waiting on God?
faqs.answer: He says God told Moses to wait “seven days,” the disciples waited before Pentecost, and about “400 years” passed after the last prophecy before God acted again; “sometimes you just gotta wait.”

faqs.question: What does he say the word translated “share” means?
faqs.answer: He says translations have “the wrong” word, and the real word means “partnership,” “it is participating,” like “the apostles doctrine and the fellowship.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And they continued steadfastly in the apostles’ doctrine and fellowship, in the breaking of bread, and in prayers.

faqs.question: What does he say about the whale and creation in six days?
faqs.answer: He says “the whale did swallow Jonah and God did create the earth in six days,” and that Genesis 1 is not a figure of speech: “he’s a supernatural God.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: But from the beginning of the creation, God ‘made them male and female.’

faqs.question: What does he say about apologetics?
faqs.answer: He says it is “a bunch of rhetoric” when used as the religious leaders did, but that “we do need apologetics by the way to help young believers understand some things,” though “you’re going to get saved by the gospel.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Jesus answered and said to them, “You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God.

faqs.question: Does he say miracles stopped when the apostles died?
faqs.answer: No. He says “it shouldn’t be put back in some era that well that was back then and it’s stopped when the apostles died, that’s a lie,” because “Christ is the same yesterday today and how long forever.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.

faqs.question: What personal story does he tell about waiting for a healing?
faqs.answer: He says he was told he was “in trouble” with a serious illness, refused the medicine, and “six months later” the doctor said “it’s gone.” He says “it happens when it happens,” and “I didn’t complain I’m just glad it happened.”
